mcq.q: Which of these is a green material for a compost heap?
mcq.explanation: Green materials are fresh and wet, such as fresh grass, peelings and fresh dung.

mcq.q: Why are diseased plants not added to compost?
options: They rot too slowly to count
They make the heap too tall
The disease can spread to the crops later
mcq.explanation: Disease germs may survive and infect crops when the compost is used.

mcq.q: About how high should a compost heap be built?
options: About as high as your chest
mcq.explanation: A heap that is too low loses heat and one that is too high is hard to turn.

mcq.q: About how long does compost usually take to be ready?
mcq.explanation: It depends on weather and materials but is usually two to three months.

mcq.q: Why should you wear gloves when handling compost materials?
options: To protect your hands from dirt and germs
mcq.explanation: Gloves protect against germs and cuts.

mcq.q: Why does drip irrigation save water?
options: It uses more water than a hose
It wets the paths between plants
Water goes close to the roots so little is wasted
mcq.explanation: Only the soil near the plant is wet, so less water is lost.

mcq.q: Where should the holes in the pipe be placed?
options: Only at the end of the row
mcq.explanation: Water must fall near the roots.

mcq.q: What should you do if a hole in a drip pipe is blocked?
options: Clear it gently with a thin wire
mcq.explanation: A thin wire clears blockages without damaging the pipe.

mcq.q: Which pupil is saving water?
options: One who waters with a drip bottle beside each plant
One who leaves the tap running
One who pours buckets over the whole bed
mcq.explanation: Drip watering is the most water-saving.

mcq.q: Why should the drip container be covered?
options: To keep out leaves and mosquitoes
mcq.explanation: A cover keeps water clean and stops mosquitoes breeding.

mcq.q: How is charcoal made?
options: By burning wood slowly with little air
mcq.explanation: Charcoal is wood partly burnt in limited air.

mcq.q: Why should food be cut into small pieces before cooking?
options: Small pieces cook faster and use less fuel
mcq.explanation: Small pieces heat through quickly.

mcq.q: What should you do if you smell gas in the kitchen?
options: Close the cylinder valve and open windows and doors
mcq.explanation: Fire near a gas leak can cause an explosion.

mcq.q: How can a family get firewood without destroying forests?
options: Plant trees on their own land and replace those cut
Cut trees from forests at night
mcq.explanation: Growing trees keeps a supply of wood.

mcq.q: Why do children need an adult when cooking?
options: Fuels and fire can burn people
mcq.explanation: Adults can guide and help prevent accidents.

mcq.q: Which crop is likely to be eaten by birds?
mcq.explanation: Birds eat ripening grain such as millet and sorghum.

mcq.q: Why are tins with pebbles tied on a scarecrow?
options: They make noise and flash to frighten animals
mcq.explanation: Noise and movement scare animals.

mcq.q: Which tool should an adult use to help fix the scarecrow pole?
options: A hammer or heavy stone to push it in
mcq.explanation: An adult helps with heavy or sharp work.

mcq.q: Which is a way of conserving wild animals?
options: Protecting their homes such as forests
mcq.explanation: Protecting habitats lets animals live.

mcq.q: Why do we use more than one method of scaring animals?
options: Animals can get used to one method
mcq.explanation: A mix of methods works better.

mcq.q: Which part holds the head of the scarecrow?
options: The dry grass on the ground
mcq.explanation: The head is fixed to the top of the long pole.

mcq.q: Which of these crops has tiny seeds sown directly?
mcq.explanation: Millet has tiny seeds that are sown where the crop stays.

mcq.q: Which tool is used to make the soil fine and level?
mcq.explanation: A rake breaks lumps and levels the bed.

mcq.q: What is a drill in sowing?
options: A shallow line in the soil where seeds are sown
mcq.explanation: A drill is a shallow furrow made with a stick.

mcq.q: What is thinning?
options: Removing extra seedlings so the rest have room
mcq.explanation: Thinning gives strong plants space.

mcq.q: Why should a container seedbed have holes at the bottom?
mcq.explanation: Waterlogged soil rots seeds and roots.

mcq.q: How do you know millet is ready to harvest?
options: The plants are green and soft
The heads turn brown and the grains are hard
mcq.explanation: Ripe grain is hard and dry.

mcq.q: Which of these fruits does best in cool highland areas?
mcq.explanation: Tree tomato grows well in cooler highlands, while coconut, cashew and mango like warm places.

mcq.q: What is a seedling?
options: A young plant grown from a seed
mcq.explanation: A seedling is a young plant.

mcq.q: What is topsoil?
options: The dark top layer of soil
mcq.explanation: Topsoil is rich in plant food.

mcq.q: Why is mulch put around a young tree?
options: It keeps the soil moist and controls weeds
mcq.explanation: Mulch reduces evaporation.

mcq.q: Why do we weed around fruit plants?
options: Weeds take water and food from the plants
mcq.explanation: Weeds compete with the crop.

mcq.q: Which is a way of protecting ripe fruit from birds and monkeys?
options: Cover trees with nets or use scare methods
mcq.explanation: Peaceful protection.

mcq.q: Which is a woody tree fruit in this lesson?
mcq.explanation: Tree tomato and guava are woody.

mcq.q: Why should the soil be firmed around a newly planted seedling?
options: To remove air spaces and hold the roots
mcq.explanation: Air pockets dry out roots.

mcq.q: Which is likely to take longest to give fruit?
mcq.explanation: Big trees like mango take several years.

mcq.q: Which practice keeps children safe when harvesting fruit?
options: Use a picking pole and take turns
mcq.explanation: Use safe methods.

mcq.q: What is the young one of a cow called?
mcq.explanation: A calf is a young cow or bull.

mcq.q: What is the meat from cattle called?
mcq.explanation: Beef comes from cattle.

mcq.q: Which of these can oxen do on a farm?
mcq.explanation: Oxen give draught power.

mcq.q: Which nutrient in eggs helps the body to grow?
mcq.explanation: Eggs are body-building foods.

mcq.q: Which of these is an indigenous chicken called in Kenya?
mcq.explanation: Kienyeji chickens are local breeds.

mcq.q: Which animal is not domestic?
mcq.explanation: Elephants are wild.

mcq.q: Which of these is an energy-giving food?
mcq.explanation: Ugali is a starchy staple.

mcq.q: Which of these fruits is a protective food?
mcq.explanation: Fruits are protective foods.

mcq.q: Why is a meal of only chips not balanced?
options: It lacks body-building and protective foods
mcq.explanation: Chips give mainly energy.

mcq.q: Which food is a good source of protein and cheap in many homes?
mcq.explanation: Beans are protein-rich.

mcq.q: Why is a food journal kept for a week?
options: To check whether meals are balanced
To count the number of plates
mcq.explanation: A journal shows patterns in eating.

mcq.q: Which meal is missing body-building foods?
mcq.explanation: Ugali and kale give energy and vitamins but no protein food.

mcq.q: Why do we cook food?
options: To make it soft, tasty and safe to eat
mcq.explanation: Heat kills germs and softens food.

mcq.q: Which food is cooked by deep frying and not shallow frying?
mcq.explanation: Mandazi float in deep oil.

mcq.q: How can you tell that water is boiling?
options: Big bubbles rise quickly and steam comes off
mcq.explanation: These are signs of boiling.

mcq.q: Why is it a good idea to use the water from boiled vegetables in soup?
options: It contains vitamins that came out of the vegetables
mcq.explanation: Some vitamins go into the cooking water.

mcq.q: How much oil is used for shallow frying?
options: A small amount that covers the bottom of the pan
mcq.explanation: Shallow frying uses a thin layer.

mcq.q: What should you do first for a small burn?
options: Cool it under running clean water for at least ten minutes
mcq.explanation: Cooling reduces burn damage.

mcq.q: Which of these foods needs a long time of boiling before it is soft enough to eat?
mcq.explanation: Dry beans are hard and need long cooking.

mcq.q: What are germs?
options: Tiny living things that can cause disease
mcq.explanation: Germs cannot be seen without a microscope.

mcq.q: Which part is often forgotten when washing hands?
options: Under the nails and between the fingers
mcq.explanation: Germs hide there.

mcq.q: How often should you brush your teeth?
mcq.explanation: Morning and before bed.

mcq.q: Why should you wear clean clothes?
options: To make the clothes wear out
Dirty clothes can carry germs and smell
mcq.explanation: Clean clothes keep us fresh.

mcq.q: Why do farmers and cleaners wear personal protective equipment?
options: To protect the body from dirt, injury and germs
mcq.explanation: PPE is clothing and gear that protects us from harm.

mcq.q: Which disease can result from drinking unsafe water?
mcq.explanation: Cholera spreads through dirty water.

mcq.q: What is domestic hygiene?
options: Keeping the home and its surroundings clean
mcq.explanation: It is care of the home environment.

mcq.q: What is the correct order for cleaning a room?
mcq.explanation: Dust falls, so dust before sweeping.

mcq.q: Where should you start mopping?
options: At the corner farthest from the door
mcq.explanation: You do not step on the clean floor.

mcq.q: How should broken glass be disposed of?
options: Wrapped in thick paper and given to an adult
mcq.explanation: This prevents cuts.

mcq.q: Why should you never mix cleaning chemicals?
options: They can give off harmful fumes
mcq.explanation: Mixing chemicals is dangerous.

mcq.q: What should you wear when handling rubbish?
mcq.explanation: Gloves protect from germs and cuts.

mcq.q: What is personal protective equipment?
options: Clothing and gear worn to protect the body
mcq.explanation: PPE protects us from harm.

mcq.q: Which PPE protects the body and clothes from dirt?
mcq.explanation: An overall covers the body.

mcq.q: What do you use to scrub gumboots?
options: A soft brush with soapy water
mcq.explanation: A soft brush avoids damage.

mcq.q: Where should canvas shoes be dried?
mcq.explanation: Gentle drying protects the shoes.

mcq.q: What should you do after cleaning PPE?
mcq.explanation: Hands can carry germs.

mcq.q: Which kind of PPE is suitable for handling compost?
mcq.explanation: They protect hands and feet.

mcq.q: What is a tacking stitch?
options: A temporary stitch that holds cloth in place
mcq.explanation: Tacking is removed later.

mcq.q: In long and short tacking, the pattern is
options: A long stitch followed by a short stitch
mcq.explanation: The pattern alternates.

mcq.q: What should you do at the end of a sewing lesson?
mcq.explanation: Counting ensures none is lost.

mcq.q: How long should a length of thread be for tacking?
options: About as long as from fingertips to elbow, up to 50 cm
mcq.explanation: Long thread tangles.

mcq.q: Which cloth is easiest for beginners?
mcq.explanation: Cotton is easy to handle.

mcq.q: How much of each edge is folded twice for the handkerchief hem?
mcq.explanation: The raw edge is hidden.

mcq.q: Which skill from Mathematics helps in tacking?
mcq.explanation: Measuring gives even and accurate stitches.

short.q: Name two things that should never be put in a compost heap and say why.
short.answer: Plastic and glass, because they do not rot.
short.working: 1 mark for two items, 1 mark for the reason.

short.q: How can you tell that compost is ready for use?
short.answer: It is dark brown, crumbly, smells like earth, and the original wastes cannot be seen.

short.q: List three things needed to make a bucket drip system.
short.answer: A bucket or container, a hose or pipe, and small holes or drippers for water to come out. A stand may also be used.

short.q: Name two other ways of saving water in the garden.
short.answer: Mulching, collecting rainwater, watering in the morning or evening, reusing wash water (any two).

short.q: Explain why we must not leave a fire burning after cooking.
short.answer: It wastes fuel and can cause a fire or accident.
short.working: 1 mark for waste, 1 mark for danger.

short.q: Why should kerosene never be poured onto a fire?
short.answer: It catches fire quickly and can burst into flames and burn people.
short.working: 1 mark for catching fire, 1 mark for danger.

short.q: List three materials that can be used to make a scarecrow.
short.answer: Sticks or poles, old clothes, a sack, dry grass, string, tins, old CDs (any three).

short.q: Explain four ways in which wild animals help people or the environment.
short.answer: Birds eat insects; bees pollinate; animals spread seeds; wildlife brings tourists and money.

short.q: Name three crops established by direct sowing of tiny seeds.
short.answer: Carrot, millet, amaranth, radish, sorghum (any three).

short.q: Explain what thinning is and why it is done.
short.answer: It is removing extra seedlings. It gives the remaining plants space and reduces competition for water, light and food.
short.working: 1 mark for meaning, 2 marks for reasons.

short.q: Explain what a fruit is in plant growth.
short.answer: The part of a plant that holds the seeds.
short.working: 1 mark for part of a plant, 1 mark for holding seeds.

short.q: Describe how to plant a fruit seedling.
short.answer: Water the seedling; remove the bag carefully; place at the same depth in the hole; fill with soil and firm; water and mulch.
short.working: 1 mark each for four correct steps.

short.q: Give three signs that fruit is ripe, naming the fruit.
short.answer: Passion fruit turns purple or yellow and wrinkles; guava turns yellowish and smells sweet; pawpaw turns yellow or orange and gives when pressed.
short.working: 1 mark for each sign with fruit.

short.q: How do fruits help our health?
short.answer: They give vitamins that fight illness, fibre that helps digestion and water that keeps the body healthy.

short.q: Give two ways of protecting fruits from birds and monkeys without killing them.
short.answer: Cover with nets, use scarecrows, noise or shiny objects (any two).

short.q: Give three uses of sheep.
short.answer: Mutton, wool (some breeds), skins, manure, income (any three).

short.q: Describe how to prepare a class talk about one domestic animal.
short.answer: Choose an animal; collect pictures; list its uses and care; practise speaking clearly; present and answer questions.

short.q: Give three benefits of eating a balanced meal.
short.answer: It gives energy, helps the body to grow and repair, and protects from illness.

short.q: How can a family get a balanced meal cheaply?
short.answer: Grow vegetables and fruits at home and use cheap proteins such as beans, omena or eggs.

short.q: State the difference between boiling and shallow frying.
short.answer: Boiling cooks food in bubbling water. Shallow frying cooks food in a thin layer of hot oil in a pan.

short.q: Describe how to boil eggs.
short.answer: Put eggs in a pot, cover with cold water, bring to the boil, boil gently for about 10 minutes, cool in cold water and peel.
short.working: 1 mark for each of four steps.

short.q: Describe the first aid for a small burn.
short.answer: Put the burn under cool running clean water for at least ten minutes, cover it loosely with a clean cloth and tell an adult.

short.q: Explain the meaning of personal hygiene.
short.answer: Keeping our own body clean to stay healthy.
short.working: 1 mark for keeping clean, 1 mark for health.

short.q: Describe how to make a tippy tap.
short.answer: Take a clean jerrican; make a small hole near the cap; hang it; tie a string from the cap to a foot lever; place a basin below and hang soap.

short.q: Give three reasons why nails should be kept short and clean.
short.answer: Germs hide under nails, worm eggs are found there, and long nails can scratch and cause injury.

short.q: Name three methods of cleaning the home environment.
short.answer: Sweeping, dusting, mopping and disposal of refuse (any three).

short.q: Name three improvised cleaning tools and what each is made from.
short.answer: Duster from old cloth; mop from strips of cloth on a stick; dustpan from a cut jerrican.
short.working: 1 mark for each tool with material.

short.q: Plan a weekly cleaning schedule for the classroom using dusting, sweeping, mopping and refuse disposal.
short.answer: A table of days with jobs for each learner group: Monday dusting, Tuesday sweeping, Wednesday mopping, and refuse disposal each day, with tools and safety measures.
short.working: 2 marks for jobs, 1 for tools, 1 for safety, 1 for fairness of sharing.

short.q: Describe how to clean canvas shoes.
short.answer: Remove laces; brush off loose dirt; scrub gently with soapy water; rinse; stuff with paper; dry in the shade.
short.working: 1 mark for each of four steps.

short.q: Explain how PPE should be stored and why.
short.answer: Clean and dry, in a cupboard, rack or clean box, so it does not grow mould or spread germs, and labelled so it is used by the owner.
short.working: 2 marks for storing, 2 marks for reasons.

short.q: Name two types of tacking stitches and describe each.
short.answer: Even tacking has equal stitches and gaps; long and short tacking has a long stitch followed by a short stitch.
short.working: 1 mark for each name and 1 for correct descriptions.

short.q: List the tools and materials needed for tacking.
short.answer: Needle, thread, scissors, ruler or tape measure, chalk, pins, cloth, thimble (any correct materials).

short.q: Why is tacking better than pins alone?
short.answer: Pins can slip or prick, tacking holds cloth firmly.
